Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team has reviewed the MSA and attached a set of redlines to the DPA and SCCs. High-level points:

- We need clarity on the processor/processor roles — Aurelius needs confirmation that Redwood will act only as a processor when processing our customer data.
- Subprocessor onboarding: we are asking for prior written consent for subprocessors that handle EU personal data (not just notice).
- Cross-border transfers: we flagged the need for a Transfer Impact Addendum given recent guidance; please confirm whether Redwood will accept the EU SCCs as executed between the parties and whether you support onward transfers to subcontractors in other regions.
- Technical measures: we need evidence of KMS usage for tenant separation and a description of key rotation and access controls.

Attached: Aurelius_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx, SCCs_comments.xlsx

Can you review and propose a path to a mutually acceptable DPA by EOD Thu (13 Jun)? If helpful, happy to do a short call to walk through.

Best,

Hi Elena — thanks for sending this and for the clear redlines. I'm looping in Ben (sales) and Monica (privacy ops) so we can coordinate legal/technical responses.

Quick responses to your bullets:
- Processor role: Redwood confirms we operate as a processor for customer workloads; we'll mark that explicitly in the DPA.
- Subprocessors: we typically provide notice with an opt-out window for specific categories, but we can discuss a limited prior-consent carveout for subprocessors that would materially change data residency or access.
- SCCs and transfer addendum: we can accept the EU SCCs as the baseline, and propose adding a short Transfer Impact Addendum annex to capture any non-EEA subprocessors and mitigations. Karthik (cc) from our legal team will advise on the exact wording.
- KMS and controls: Monica will pull the KMS diagram and key rotation statement, and we'll attach SOC 2 Type II and encryption notes.

We will produce a proposed DPA redline for your review by Wed morning (11 Jun) and are open to a call Wed afternoon or Thu morning. Which time works for you?

Team — forwarding Aurelius redlines (see below). Summary of asks and proposed approach:

1) Processor confirmation: we should add a short definitions section that explicitly states Redwood is a processor under the Agreement and will act on customer instructions.
2) Subprocessor consent: Aurelius is asking for prior written consent for subprocessors handling EU data. Proposed compromise: keep our standard notice + 14-day objection window, but add a tiered carveout for subprocessors that will store data outside the EEA or provide access to plaintext — in those cases we will (a) notify and (b) obtain explicit consent or put in place additional safeguards (SCCs + contractual commitments).
3) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): Karthik, can you draft a short TIA annex template that references our SCCs implementation, specific mitigations (encryption at-rest/in-transit, KMS tenant separation, contractual controls), and the subprocessor list? Also include language on remediation/mitigations if the TIA indicates elevated risk.
4) Evidence package: Monica to assemble: SOC 2 Type II summary, KMS diagram, key rotation cadence, and the redwood_subprocessor_register.csv.

Attachments I'll prepare for the customer: Redwood_DPA_Proposal_v1.docx (tracked changes), initial TIA notes (TIA_initial_notes.pdf). Please review and send any OSH (one-sentence-holder) comments by EOB Tue so I can finalize the set for Elena.

Onwards: Ben, please confirm if this scope impacts pricing/discounts in RDW-3421 (I suspect not but worth confirming).

Thanks — Laura

Hi Elena — attached is our proposed DPA redline (Redwood_DPA_Proposal_v1.docx). Below is an executive summary of the changes and next steps so you have everything in one place.

Executive summary of proposed changes
- Processor role: explicit definition added under Section 1.1 confirming Redwood acts as a Processor and processes data per Customer instructions.
- Subprocessors: we retained notice + 14-day objection window as our baseline. For subprocessors that will store or access EU personal data outside the EEA, we added an addendum process: Redwood will either (a) obtain prior written consent for that specific subprocessor or (b) implement contractually enforceable SCCs and documented mitigations. This is intended to address Aurelius' request while preserving our operational flexibility.
- Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): included as Annex B. The TIA references our SCCs implementation, lists current subprocessors, and documents mitigations (encryption, KMS tenant separation, access controls, logging). It also contains a simple remediation path if a future TIA indicates elevated risk.
- Evidence: Monica attached a short evidence packet (SOC2 summary + KMS notes). We can also provide a redacted Subprocessor Register on request and a scoped SOC 2 bridge letter if needed for procurement.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Proposal_v1.docx, TIA_initial_notes.pdf, SOC2_summary.pdf

Proposed next steps
1) Please review the attached DPA redline and TIA annex and mark any critical objections by Thu EOD (13 Jun).
2) If preferred, let's schedule a 30-min call to go through the TIA and subprocessors — available slots: Thu 13 Jun 10:00-11:30 PT or Fri 14 Jun 09:00-12:00 PT. Book here: https://calendly.com/laura-bennett/redwood-aurelius-dpa-call.
3) If we agree, we can prepare an execution copy and loop in procurement for order form sign-off (deal RDW-3421).

If there are particular SCC clauses you want reworded rather than an annex, flag them and Karthik will work with your counsel directly.

Best,
